reasons: The cited text (three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay 'without reduction or termination rights') squarely matches the MINCOMMIT walk-away position, so a deviation finding is correctly classified.

The redline is directionally correct for the Customer: it removes the take-or-pay obligation entirely and confirms Fees are owed only for Services ordered and actually used, which is the playbook preferred position.

The high changed-character ratio (0.882) is justified here because the rule contemplates deletion or wholesale narrowing of the commitment clause; replacing the sentence with an affirmative 'no minimum commitment' statement is a defensible equivalent to deletion and preserves clause structure.

The comment is concise, first-person plural, prefixed correctly, states what changed and why, and offers the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty) as required.

Minor, non-disqualifying: the comment and redline rely on cross-references (§ 9.4, § 12.3, defined term 'Fees') that are not in the supplied excerpt — worth a quick confirmation that those sections exist as characterised before sending.
